amendments.reason: c3 could not PASS as written: it matched the literal verdict string APPROVE, while the reviewer handoff frozen at the same seam prescribes ACCEPT / ACCEPT WITH FINDINGS / REJECT. Admiral ruled amend, not waive -- a waiver hides the bug and leaves the gate permanently unpassable for every future reviewer following that handoff; an amend makes the check TRUE rather than SKIPPED. WHICH VERDICTS PASS AND WHICH FAIL: ACCEPT passes; ACCEPT WITH FINDINGS passes; REJECT FAILS. ROOT CAUSE, and it is why the fix is shaped this way: artifact-kind match is EXACT EQUALITY per key (checklist_engine.py ~line 850: all(ev.payload[k] == v for k,v in want.items())). It cannot express 'one of', which is precisely why the original author hard-coded a single verdict string and why the mismatch was possible at all. So the two accepting verdicts are normalized into one key: verdict_class ACCEPTED covers ACCEPT and ACCEPT WITH FINDINGS, while REJECT normalizes to REJECTED and fails the equality. The literal reviewer verdict is still carried verbatim in the payload's verdict field for audit -- the normalization is additive, not a replacement. THE CHECK REMAINS FAILABLE, which was the Admiral's binding condition: it is NOT loosened to accept any verdict string, which would convert a check that cannot pass into a check that cannot fail -- the same defect wearing the other mask, shipped inside the wave hunting it. It is guarded twice over: a REJECT fails on verdict_class, and independently fails on blocking_findings=0, since a REJECT necessarily carries at least one blocking finding. An ACCEPT WITH FINDINGS that carried blocking findings would also, correctly, fail. Check KIND is unchanged (artifact->artifact), as retext-check requires.
